Description: Answer code this marker applies to. Matches response.code and historical_response.code. Deliberately not a foreign key - see the note in V1_14 about the reference tables.

What the answer indicates: SERIOUS_INJURY, SEXUAL_ASSAULT, MEDICAL_TREATMENT_REQUIRED, HOSPITAL_ADMISSION, TRANSMITTABLE_INFECTIOUS_DISEASE, SALIVA_HIT_BODY, HIT_NECK_OR_ABOVE or WEAPON_URINE. Note that this table says which answers are serious, not which reports were - joining it to response is what makes a report's content special category, not this table on its own.
The outcome code as stored in prisoner_involvement.outcome.
Display order for the outcome.
Human-readable name of the outcome.
The role code as stored in prisoner_involvement.prisoner_role.
Display order for the role.
Human-readable name of the role.
The role code as stored in staff_involvement.staff_role.
Display order for the role.
Human-readable name of the role.
The status code as stored in report.status and status_history.status, for example DRAFT or AWAITING_REVIEW.
Display order for the status.
Short human-readable name of the status.

Whether downstream consumers should skip reports in this status. True for DUPLICATE, NOT_REPORTABLE, REOPENED and WAS_CLOSED - reports that would otherwise be double-counted or counted when they should not be. Anything aggregating reports should honour this.
Fuller plain-English explanation of what the status means, shown to users and useful when interpreting a status trail. Added in V1_46.
Example Value: A report that has been submitted for the first time and is now ready for review.

Description: The type code as stored in report.type and history.type, for example SELF_HARM_1 or ASSAULT_5.
Display order for the type.
Human-readable name of the type.
Whether the type can be chosen for new reports. Retired types stay in the table so existing reports still decode.
The family this type belongs to, matching constant_type_family.code. Types were regrouped into families in V1_16 and their codes renamed to match, so codes on old and new reports differ.
The family code, as referenced by constant_type.family_code.
Display order for the family.
Human-readable name of the family.
The action code as stored in correction_request.user_action and report.last_user_action.
Display order for the action.
Human-readable name of the action.
The user type code as stored in correction_request.user_type: REPORTING_OFFICER or DATA_WARDEN.
Display order for the user type.
Human-readable name of the user type.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report this request concerns. Foreign key to report.id.

Free-text description of what was asked for or done, written by hand. Quotes and summarises the report's content, so assume it carries the same health, offending and third-party detail as the description itself.
Example Value: Please add the names of the staff who attended.

Description: When the request was made or the action recorded.
Username of the member of staff who made the request or took the action. Identifies a member of staff.
Order of this request within the report's trail.

Agency (prison) code or PECS region the requester was working in. Read with correction_requested_by it indicates where that member of staff was based. Nullable on older rows written before the column existed.
What the user did, for example REQUEST_REVIEW, REQUEST_CORRECTION, RECALL or CLOSE. Values are in constant_user_action. Null on rows written before the column existed.
Reference of the report this one was found to duplicate, recorded when it is marked as a duplicate. A report_reference rather than an id, and null on every other row.

Which kind of user acted: REPORTING_OFFICER or DATA_WARDEN. The two have different permissions, so this records the capacity someone acted in rather than their job title. Values are in constant_user_type. Null on rows written before the column existed.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report this addendum belongs to. Foreign key to report.id.
Order of this addendum within the report. Read in this order after report.description.
The added text. Carries the same sensitivity as report.description - written by hand, and in practice describing injuries, health, offending and named third parties.
Example Value: Prisoner later said the injury happened in a fall.

Description: When the addendum was added.
Username of the member of staff who added it. Identifies a member of staff.
First name of the member of staff who added it, snapshotted at the time.
Last name of the member of staff who added it, snapshotted at the time.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The type-change snapshot this question belongs to. Foreign key to history.id - the equivalent of question.report_id one level removed.
Order the question was asked in.

The business key for the question in the question set that applied before the report's type was changed. As question.code: says which question was asked, and does not change when the wording is corrected.

The question in the legacy form NOMIS held, as it stood before the report's type was changed. As question.question: often in capitals or misspelt, or a key such as lock_type for some newer incident types. Not for display - label is the wording the user saw. Expected to be removed once NOMIS is switched off. Form wording rather than an answer.
Free text the reporter added against the question. Written by hand, so assume it carries health, offending and third-party detail.
Example Value: Treatment refused at first, accepted later.

Description: The question exactly as it was shown to the user, before the report's type was changed. As question.label: the wording to display, stored so the form can be reconstructed as it was presented. Form wording rather than an answer.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The historical question this answers. Foreign key to historical_question.id.
Order of this answer within the question's answers.

The answer in the legacy form NOMIS held, as it stood before the report's type was changed. As response.response: often in capitals or misspelt, or a key for some newer incident types. Not for display - label is the wording the user saw. Expected to be removed once NOMIS is switched off. Still records what happened in the incident about the people named on the report.
Date given as the answer, where the question asked for one. Null on answers that are not dates.
Free text the reporter added against this answer. Written by hand, so assume it carries health, offending and third-party detail.
When the answer was recorded - the original recording, not the snapshot.
Username of the member of staff who recorded the answer. Identifies a member of staff.

The business key for the answer chosen, in the question set that applied before the report's type was changed. As response.code: does not change when the wording is corrected. Discloses what was answered.

The answer exactly as it was shown to the user, before the report's type was changed. As response.label: the wording to display, stored so the form can be reconstructed as it was presented. Records what happened in the incident about the people named on the report.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report this snapshot belongs to. Foreign key to report.id.

The incident type the report held before it was changed - so a report now typed ASSAULT_5 may have a history row typed SELF_HARM_1. Carries the same sensitivity as report.type, and note that it discloses what the incident was once believed to be. Values are in constant_type.
When the type was changed, and therefore when this snapshot was taken.
Username of the member of staff who changed the type. Identifies a member of staff.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report this involvement belongs to. Foreign key to report.id.
NOMIS offender number (noms id) of the prisoner. The link that makes this row, and much of the report, personal data about that prisoner.

How the prisoner was involved, for example VICTIM, SUSPECTED_ASSAILANT, ACTIVE_INVOLVEMENT or PRESENT_AT_SCENE. On an assault or a find of illicit items, recording someone as a suspected assailant is an allegation of offending in custody against a named person - criminal offence data under Article 10, which DPA 2018 s.11(2) extends to alleged offences. Values are in constant_prisoner_role.

What happened to the prisoner as a result, for example PLACED_ON_REPORT, CHARGED_BY_POLICE, LOCAL_INVESTIGATION or TRANSFER. Records criminal or disciplinary proceedings against a named person. Null where no outcome has been recorded. Values are in constant_prisoner_outcome.

Free-text note on this prisoner's involvement. Unstructured and written by hand - in practice describes injuries, behaviour, health and other people, so treat as special category regardless of what any individual comment happens to say.
Example Value: Minor injury to the hand, seen by healthcare.

Description: Order of this prisoner within the report's list. Display order only.
Prisoner's first name as at the time the report was written. A snapshot copied from the prisoner search API, not kept in step afterwards.
Prisoner's last name as at the time the report was written. A snapshot copied from the prisoner search API, not kept in step afterwards.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report this question belongs to. Foreign key to report.id, and unique with code - a question is asked at most once per report.
Order the question was asked in.

The business key for the question: says which question in the incident type's question set was asked. The question sets are configured in the incident reporting front end. Wording is corrected over time but the code does not change, so it is the key for analysing answers across reports.

The question in the legacy form NOMIS held. For questions that came from NOMIS this is often in capitals, with spelling mistakes and missing punctuation, and is kept unchanged because systems downstream may process on it. Some newer incident types hold a key such as lock_type here rather than a sentence. Not for display - label is the wording the user saw. Expected to be removed once NOMIS is switched off. Form wording rather than an answer, so not personal data in itself.
Free text the reporter added against the question rather than against a specific answer. Written by hand, so assume it carries health, offending and third-party detail.
Example Value: Treatment refused at first, accepted later.

Description: The question exactly as it was shown to the user completing the report, at the time they answered it. Wording is corrected from time to time - spelling, punctuation - so it is stored with each report, so the form can be reconstructed as it was presented. This is the wording to display. Form wording rather than an answer, so not personal data in itself.
Primary key. Time-ordered UUID v7, so insert order matches id order. Internal - the reference people quote is report_reference.
Human-readable reference for the report, unique across the service. Known as the "incident number" in NOMIS, and the identifier staff quote to each other. Identifies an incident, not a person.

Short title for the incident. For reports created in DPS it is generated automatically from the incident type, the prison number and surname of every prisoner involved and the prison, so it names everyone on the report. Reports that came from NOMIS carry the title the reporter wrote, which in practice often names people or summarises what happened.

The reporter's account of what happened. Unstructured and unbounded, and the single richest source of sensitive data in the schema - it routinely describes injuries, self-harm, health treatment, offending and third parties by name. Later additions are appended as rows in description_addendum rather than edited into this column.
Example Value: Officer found the prisoner in their cell with a cut to the forearm. Healthcare attended.

Description: Agency (prison) code where the incident happened. Read with prisoner_involvement it indicates where those prisoners were held at the time. Renamed from prison_id in V1_2 and widened, because PECS regions are also valid values here - a report is not always tied to an establishment.

What kind of incident this is, for example SELF_HARM_1, DEATH_OTHER_1, ASSAULT_5 or FIND_6. Drives which questions are asked. This is Article 9 or Article 10 data about everyone named on the report whichever value it holds - that a report exists and is a self-harm report discloses health data about the prisoner it concerns. Values are listed in constant_type and grouped by constant_type_family.
Where the report was first created: DPS or NOMIS. Reports migrated or synchronised from NOMIS carry NOMIS.

Where the report has got to in the workflow, for example DRAFT, AWAITING_REVIEW, ON_HOLD, NEEDS_UPDATING, CLOSED or DUPLICATE. Values and their meanings are in constant_status, which also records which statuses downstream consumers should ignore.
When the incident happened, as reported. Distinct from reported_at, which is when someone wrote it up - the gap between the two is often days.
When the incident was reported. For reports synchronised from NOMIS this is the original NOMIS value, not the sync.
Username of the member of staff who reported the incident. Identifies a member of staff.
Legacy NOMIS question set identifier, carried over in the original schema and never used since - no Kotlin code reads or writes it, and it is not exposed by the API. Treat as dead.
When the row was created in this service. For reports synchronised from NOMIS this is the sync, not the incident or the original report - use incident_date_and_time or reported_at for those.
Username of the member of staff who last changed the report, or the system user for changes made by the NOMIS sync. Identifies a member of staff.
When the report was last changed.
Which system made the last change: DPS or NOMIS. A report can be created in one and edited in the other, so this is not the same as source.
Whether the reporter has finished recording staff involvement. Distinguishes "no staff were involved" from "not yet filled in", which an empty staff_involvement cannot do on its own.
Whether the reporter has finished recording prisoner involvement. Distinguishes "no prisoners were involved" from "not yet filled in", which an empty prisoner_involvement cannot do on its own.
The report this one duplicates, set when it is marked DUPLICATE. Points at report.id, not report_reference. Null on every report that is not a duplicate.

The most recent action taken on the report through a correction request, denormalised here so a list of reports can show it without joining. Mirrors the newest correction_request.user_action and is null until the first one.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The question this answers. Foreign key to question.id.
Order of this answer within the question's answers.

The answer in the legacy form NOMIS held. For answers that came from NOMIS this is often in capitals, with spelling mistakes and missing punctuation, and is kept unchanged because systems downstream may process on it. Some newer incident types hold a key such as who_identified_the_error_court here rather than words. Not for display - label is the wording the user saw. Expected to be removed once NOMIS is switched off. Still records what happened in the incident - injuries, weapons, methods, whether the police attended - about the people named on the report.
Date given as the answer, where the question asks for one - for example when a death occurred or when treatment was given. Null on answers that are not dates.
Free text the reporter added against this answer. Written by hand, so assume it carries health, offending and third-party detail.
When the answer was recorded.
Username of the member of staff who recorded the answer. Identifies a member of staff.

The business key for the answer: says which of the answers offered to the question was chosen. The answers offered are configured in the incident reporting front end with the questions. Wording is corrected over time but the code does not change, so it is the key for analysing answers across reports, and the key analytical_marker uses to flag answers that indicate serious harm. Discloses what was answered, so it is as sensitive as the wording.

The answer exactly as it was shown to the user completing the report, at the time they chose it. Wording is corrected from time to time - spelling, punctuation - so it is stored with each report, so the form can be reconstructed as it was presented. This is the wording to display. Records what happened in the incident about the people named on the report.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report this involvement belongs to. Foreign key to report.id.
DPS username of the member of staff. Nullable since V1_15: staff can be named on a report without having a DPS account, in which case only the names are recorded. Identifies a member of staff.

How the member of staff was involved, for example WITNESS, FIRST_ON_SCENE, ACTIVELY_INVOLVED or SUSPECTED_INVOLVEMENT. Note that SUSPECTED_INVOLVEMENT is an allegation against a named member of staff and is sensitive well beyond an ordinary audit field - tagged STAFF rather than SPECIAL-CATEGORY so staff data stays separable, but handle it accordingly. Values are in constant_staff_role.

Free-text note on this member of staff's involvement. Unstructured and written by hand - describes what they did or what happened to them, and routinely names prisoners and describes injuries, so treat as special category.
Example Value: First to arrive and called for healthcare.

Description: Order of this member of staff within the report's list. Display order only.
Member of staff's first name as at the time the report was written. A snapshot, not kept in step afterwards.
Member of staff's last name as at the time the report was written. A snapshot, not kept in step afterwards.
Primary key. Surrogate sequence value.
The report whose status changed. Foreign key to report.id.
The status the report moved into. Values and their meanings are in constant_status.
When the status changed.
Username of the member of staff who changed it, or the system user for automatic transitions. Identifies a member of staff.
